title: Egress handoff latency aftershock - debug journal
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad for the weird latency spikes after the us-east1->eu-west1 handoff yesterday (post-rollout). Personal log so expect half sentences and repeated ideas.

Timeline (short):
- 2024-03-14 10:12 UTC: Canary rollout of routing policy v2 -> traffic steering by latency and cost.
- 2024-03-14 10:45 UTC: Observability alert: per-request P50 latency for /v1/generate in us-east1 cluster climbed from ~85ms to ~420ms for ~8min windows.
- 2024-03-14 10:47 UTC: Auto-fallback triggered: smart-routing policy moved 12% of traffic to eu-west1 model-quant-sm (fallback variant).
- 2024-03-14 10:53 UTC: Latency returned to baseline once fallback stabilized. Postmort shows a small tail of 5xxs and slow tails repeated for 30m.

What I saw in logs (important snippets):
- From edge-proxy logs (us-east1 edge):
  - 2024-03-14T10:46:02Z ERROR route-eval - routePolicyEvaluator: candidateLatencyMultiple=3.9, chosen=eu-west1, fallback_reason=capacity-pressure
  - 2024-03-14T10:46:03Z WARN egress-proxy - tls-handshake=failed, err=EOF, remote_ip=34.101.12.23
  - 2024-03-14T10:47:11Z INFO cache - kv-cache-miss model:openlp-3b, key=prefix-...

- From eu-west1 serving logs (instance-side):
  - 2024-03-14T10:46:05Z INFO serve - accept conn from 10.8.32.45, client-region=us-east1-edge-02
  - 2024-03-14T10:46:06Z ERROR generator - tokenizer mismatch: model=openlp-3b-q8, request-encoder=avx2-v2 (falling back to cpu-encode)
  - 2024-03-14T10:46:09Z ERROR http - 503 Service Unavailable: upstream concurrency exceeded

Commands I ran (repro / ad-hoc probes):
- curl to edge with headers forcing region reroute:
  curl -i -X POST https://edge.us-east1.redwood/api/generate -H 'x-region-preference: eu-west1' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
  -> sometimes 200 in 120-450ms, sometimes 503/504 around 2-6s. High variance.

- tcpdump on node us-east1-edge-02 (short):
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 34.101.12.23 and port 443 -w handoff.pcap
  Observed many TCP retransmits and occasional TLS renegotiation attempts.

- JWKS/key rotation sanity check:
  curl -s https://auth.eu-west1.redwood/.well-known/jwks.json | jq '.keys | length'
  -> correct, no rotation event logged in auth-service during the window.

- K8s describe on serving pod (eu-west1):
  kubectl -n serving describe pod model-openlp-3b-q8-57b9
  -> Events show oomKills ~1 week ago, restarted 2 days ago, readiness probe flapped once at 2024-03-14T08:12:xx (preceding maintenance).

Hypotheses (ranked / quick):
1) Cold KV cache + cross-region handoff: when the edge routes to eu-west1 it needs to warm prefix KV and tokenizer caches; cache-miss + tokenizer fallback caused CPU path and higher latency. Evidence: kv-cache-miss logs and tokenizer mismatch message.
2) TLS connection churn between regions: edge sees EOF/TLS handshake fails -> causes retries and long tails. Evidence: tcpdump retransmits and tls-handshake=failed logs.
3) Serving instance concurrency cap reached for fallback model variant (quantized variant has lower concurrency or different scheduler), leading to 503s. Evidence: 503 upstream concurrency exceeded.
4) Policy configuration bug: new smart-routing tiering incorrectly set weight thresholds that push too much traffic to smaller eu-west1 pool under transient load. Evidence: rollback to previous policy removed the spike in one test.
5) NAT gateway / egress bandwidth limits in eu-west1 zone -> transient queuing. Evidence: thin. Need cloud provider metrics.

Immediate actions taken during incident: 
- Rolled back smart-routing policy v2 to v1 at 10:55 UTC (mitigated).
- Scoped fallback thresholds to reduce aggressive cross-region shift in canary group.
- Created MC-3421 and pinned the eu-west1 fallback pool to increase concurrency.
- Collected pcap and stack traces and uploaded to shared artifacts (see linked_artifacts).

Reproduction notes (how to trigger locally / staging):
- Use a small bucket model in us-east1 and a quantized variant in eu-west1.
- Simulate prefix cache cold start by purging kv-cache (admin API: POST /admin/kv/flush with model param).
- From an edge node, trigger route change header: 'x-route-shift: eu-west1' and flood with steady QPS ~30 RPS for 2-5m to observe stair-step latency.

Commands to run in staging (checklist):
- curl -v -H 'x-route-shift: eu-west1' https://staging-edge.us-east1.redwood/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"warmup"}'
- while curl runs, tail logs: sudo journalctl -u edge-proxy -f | grep -E "tls-handshake|route-eval|kv-cache"
- on eu-west1 serving node: sudo perf top (sample) and dmesg -T | tail -n 40 to see OOM/oomkiller signs
- cloud metrics: query GCE/NODE egress bytes, TCP retransmits, and NAT gateway Saturation

Open questions / things to validate:
- Did the rollout coincide with any kernel/security patches on eu-west1 nodes? (check image-version tags)
- Are tokenizers compiled with matching CPU flags across regions? We saw an "avx2-v2" vs fallback to cpu-encode. If compile flags differ we get slower path.
- Confirm per-model concurrency settings for quantized variants; they may have lower max inflight due to memory constraints.
- Where is the TLS termination happening? Edge -> edge-proxy -> regional serving. If TLS handoff is being re-established between edge-proxy and regional serving frequently, we need to make TLS persistent or reuse connections more aggressively.

Notes for follow-ups / TODO (short):
- [ ] Add synthetic test that exercises cross-region fallback under cold-KV conditions (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Add telemetry for TLS handshake time per connection (owner: Jonah).
- [ ] Run a canary that pins tokenizer build flags across regions (owner: Evan).
- [ ] Increase reserved concurrency on eu-west1 fallback pool temporarily (on-call ops).
- [ ] Check cloud provider NAT gateway egress metrics and open support ticket if pronounced (MC-3440).

Random breadcrumbs/observations that might matter:
- Some requests that hit eu-west1 had x-client-ttl header ~45s, others 300s. Not sure why TTL differs; could be fronted CDN setting.
- A small fraction of requests got routed to a model variant labeled "-compat"; logs show a slow path on these.
- When I forced keep-alive connections from the edge to eu-west1 (reuse), observed fewer TLS errors in a quick manual test.

Quick verdict for incident report draft: 
Primary cause likely multi-factor: tokenizer/kv-cold-start (high Latency) + TLS churn (retries) amplified by an aggressive routing policy that shifted too much traffic to a lower-capacity fallback pool.
Secondary: potential infra egress/persistence (NAT/TCP) contributing to retransmit tail.

If I get time: assemble timeline with request ids and correlate edge->serving spans in traces (trace ids are in edge logs). That will make RCA crisp.

End of scratch log. Will convert into incident timeline + RCA once I correlate traces.
